observations.title: The repository documents its own architecture in-tree
observations.question: Read these before writing anything about this repository's architecture. Which of them state a convention that is a correctness requirement rather than a style preference, and which name a footgun a newcomer would hit? Anything already written here belongs in AGENTS.md as a CITATION, never as a paraphrase that will drift from the original.
observations.draft_rule: Before changing `<area>`, read `<doc path>` — it is the authored convention for this subsystem. State the constraint it carries (`<constraint>`) and cite the document rather than restating it here.

observations.title: This repository participates in the G/M-code command contract
observations.question: Does this repository SEND, FORWARD or HANDLE these codes? A code is a contract shared by every repository on its path — which sibling has the parser, which has the dispatcher, and which document is the registry of record?
observations.draft_rule: Adding or changing a G/M-code is an ecosystem change, never a local one. Register the code and its parameter definitions in `<registry path>` and synchronise the parser, dispatch and handler in `<sibling repos>` in the same ticket. Load `ultimaker-gcode-architecture` before touching a code; do not restate the registry in this repository. Relevant catalogue skills: `ultimaker-gcode-architecture`.

observations.title: A WebAssembly/embind boundary crosses out of this repository
observations.question: Which link options and exported symbols are a published contract with the JavaScript consumer, and which are build trivia? Which consumer bundler configuration depends on them, and is any generated TypeScript surface (`.d.ts`, a generated registry) typechecked by anything at all?
observations.draft_rule: The Emscripten link options in `<file>` are a contract with `<consumer repo>`'s bundler, not a build detail: `<contractual flags>` determine how the module is imported and must not change without naming the consumer impact in the PR. WASM-specific code stays in `<wasm dir>`; the core must build natively unchanged. Every exported binding is a public API change. Relevant catalogue skills: `ultimaker-curator-development`, `ultimaker-neoprep-development`.

observations.title: This repository's public surface is mounted into other repositories
evidence: no entry point starts a process here, yet the repository publishes a surface (`include/`)
observations.question: Which consumers pin this repository, and what is the ordering discipline for a change that spans both trees? Rule 34 states the part that is provable from this tree; the rest belongs here.
observations.draft_rule: Every exported symbol, model field and schema in the published surface is a contract with the repositories that mount it. Land the change here first, then move each consumer's pointer; prefer additive shape changes and name the consumers in the pull request.

reasons: no entry point starts a process here, yet the repository publishes a surface (`include/`)

observations.title: Tests are collected in a top-level test tree
evidence: 5 test files: 5 in a central tree, 0 beside sources
observations.question: Should the test-placement convention be stated so agents stop guessing where a new test belongs?
observations.draft_rule: Place new tests in the top-level test tree, mirroring the source directory structure.

observations.title: Commit messages carry explanatory bodies
evidence: 54% of sampled commits have a body
observations.question: Should agents be required to write a body explaining why/how, not just a subject line?
observations.draft_rule: Every commit message MUST include a body explaining why the change was needed and how it works — a subject line alone is not enough.

observations.title: Commits are small and tightly scoped
observations.question: Should the scope rule name a concrete file-count expectation derived from this repository's own history?
observations.draft_rule: Keep commits tightly scoped: this repository's median commit touches 1 files. A commit touching more than 3 files needs an explicit justification in the message.

observations.title: This repository publishes a package whose identity is generated, not committed
observations.question: What is the published artifact called, who consumes it, and where does its version string actually come from? A repository whose package metadata is generated at packaging time has no committed manifest for a detector to read — the identity has to be traced through the recipe.
observations.draft_rule: The published artifact is `<package name>`, assembled by `<mechanism>`; `<file>` is the single source of truth for its identity, version and exports. Never hand-write a competing manifest. Consumers (`<consumer repos>`) pin exact versions — a breaking change to the exported surface requires the paired consumer PR in the same ticket. Relevant catalogue skills: `conan-2`.

observations.title: History keeps merge commits
evidence: 63/300 sampled commits are merges (mostly pull request merges)
observations.question: Is the merge commit intentional (preserving branch topology), and should agents therefore NOT rebase published branches?
observations.draft_rule: This repository preserves merge topology. Do not rewrite or rebase branches that have already been pushed; integrate with merges.

observations.title: Observed file-size distribution (input to the ratchet)
evidence: 1 of 43 sampled files exceed the 400-line budget and will be grandfathered at their current size
observations.question: The file-size ratchet is already generated as a managed rule (`10-file-size-and-decomposition-rules.md`) with a 400-line budget. Is 400 the right budget for this codebase, or does its shape justify a different number (90th percentile is 134)? Re-run the bootstrap with `--file-size-budget N` to change it — do not write a competing rule.
observations.draft_rule: No new rule needed: adjust the managed budget instead. Consider whether the largest grandfathered files deserve a decomposition ticket of their own.

observations.title: File names are predominantly snake_case
observations.question: Does the convention differ per language or per directory, and is it worth stating so new files match?
observations.draft_rule: Name new source files in snake_case, matching the existing tree.

observations.title: Releases are tagged with bare semantic versions
observations.question: Do version bumps have a required home (packaging metadata, recipe file, CMake project version) that must move together with the tag?
observations.draft_rule: Release tags follow bare semantic versions. When bumping a version, update every location that carries it (<list them>) in the same commit.
